title: Exactness of constructed kernel boundary at kernel tensor
statement: For every commutative ring R, modules M,F,N and surjective q:F → N, the constructed boundary has exactness of (δ_q,inclusion tensor 1_M).

proof.text: Let P be the chosen projective resolution of N, d its degree-one differential, epsilon its augmentation, e the augmentation lift through q, K = ker(q), i its inclusion and D the restriction of e d to K. Define s:K × P0 -> F by s(k,p)=i(k)+e(p), and j:P1 -> K × P0 by j(z)=(D(z),-d(z)). The augmentation epsilon is surjective, so s is surjective: lift q(f) to p and use (f-e(p),p). The pair (j,s) is exact: if i(k)+e(p)=0, then epsilon(p)=0, so exactness of the projective resolution at P0 gives z with d(z)=p; then j(-z)=(k,p). Conversely s(j(z))=0 by the definition of D. All these maps and identities are explicit local constructions in the Lean proof, using Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.exact₀ and the module-category exactness criterion.

Apply tensor right exactness to the surjective map s and the exact pair (j,s). If x in K tensor M is killed by i tensor 1, its image under the tensored product inclusion a(k)=(k,0) is killed by s tensor 1. Obtain z in P1 tensor M with (j tensor 1)(z)=(a tensor 1)(x). Applying the tensored first projection yields (D tensor 1)(z)=x; applying the tensored second projection yields (d tensor 1)(z)=0. These calculations use the functoriality of rTensor, and its compatibility with negation, zero and identity.

The cycles inclusion is a kernel of the tensored differential, so lift z to a cycle w. The cokernel defining torKernelHomologyBoundary gives homologyπ followed by that boundary equal to iCycles followed by D tensor 1. Therefore the homology class of w has boundary x. Apply the inverse of P.isoLeftDerivedObj to this class to obtain t in Tor1(N,M). The inverse-hom identity and the defining cycle formula show torKernelBoundary(t)=x.

For the other implication, the identity D followed by i equals d followed by e tensors to the corresponding identity. Precomposition with iCycles kills d tensor 1, so every cycle boundary is killed by i tensor 1. Since homologyπ is epic, this identity descends to torKernelHomologyBoundary. Precompose with the resolution identification of Tor to see that every value of torKernelBoundary is killed by the tensored inclusion. The two implications give Function.Exact. The unit statement and route are unchanged; only the node-level horseshoe comparison has been replaced by this explicit presentation chase.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean proof by the explicit presentation P1 -> ker(q) × P0 -> F, tensor right exactness, and the constructed cycle-to-homology boundary. The presentation chase is written by this worker; the source Tor theorem is read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M0. No unproved dependency or new statement is used.

    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (F N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (q : F →ₗ[R] N) (hq : Function.Surjective q) :
    Function.Exact (torKernelBoundary M F N q hq)
      ((LinearMap.ker q).subtype.rTensor M)
